label: input n in the first five original positions
explanation: Fires only when the input token is the letter n during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at positions t=0..4. Magnitude depends on position: highest at t=1 (about 1.0 of max), close behind at t=0 and t=2 (about 0.9-0.95), then lower at t=3 (about 0.6) and t=4 (about 0.25). It does not fire at all for n at t>=5, and only about 127 times in the whole copy phase. It never fires on the <DEL> step or on any other token. Repeated n tokens in this window still fire, so it does not need n to be a first occurrence.

issues: None of the misses are systematic. On test, all 119 missed activations are in the copy phase, where the input is an n being fed back. Their magnitudes are about 0.02-0.08 of max and together they carry 0.0% of the activation mass. They match the claim of about 127 copy-phase activations (127 on dev). There are 0 false positives on test (precision 1.0, recall 0.9985, F1 0.9993, mass recall 0.99992).

The magnitude claims check out against the dev profile. Mean activation by position, relative to t=1: t=0 is about 0.92, t=2 about 0.96, t=3 about 0.63 and t=4 about 0.22. The firing rate is the same at every original position 0-4 (about 0.033) and is 0 at original positions 5 and later. The feature never fires on the <DEL> step, and only an input of n ever activates it (100% of mass).

Minor nuance: the activations at t=5 and later in the profile are all copy-phase steps (orig_idx -1), not original positions. The cutoff is really original position 4 or earlier, which within the original phase is the same as t<=4.
Scope note: the user's request was about estimating batch 2's duration and launching batch 3. This subagent task only covered the feature interpretation, so that request still needs to be handled.
